error.signature: AI tells someone in Turkey that a building's iskan (occupancy permit) or a recent construction date means it is earthquake-safe

verdict.summary: An occupancy permit (iskan) or a post-2000 construction date is not reliable proof that a Turkish building meets earthquake-resistant standards. A 2018 zoning/construction amnesty (imar barisi, Law No. 7143) let millions of non-compliant structures obtain retroactive legal status for a fee without a genuine structural safety review, and many amnestied buildings collapsed in the February 2023 earthquakes. Owners and tenants can instead request an independent 'riskli yapi' (risky-building) structural assessment from a Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change-licensed institution under Law No. 6306.

dead_ends.action: Treat having an iskan (occupancy/habitation permit) as proof the building meets earthquake-resistant construction standards
dead_ends.why_fails: Turkey's 2018 construction amnesty (imar barisi, Law No. 7143) let over 10 million non-compliant structures - including ones with structural code violations - obtain legal status and permits retroactively for a fee, without a genuine engineering safety review. Investigations after the February 2023 Kahramanmaras earthquakes found that many buildings legalized under the amnesty, and buildings whose contractors had permits, collapsed; Turkish authorities detained and investigated hundreds of contractors and property owners over collapsed buildings.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Having legal paperwork (an occupancy permit) is conflated with structural engineering compliance; the permit records legal status, not verified seismic safety.

dead_ends.action: Assume a newer-looking building, or one built after Turkey's 1999 earthquake code reforms, automatically meets the current Turkish Earthquake Code (TBDY)
dead_ends.why_fails: Reporting on the 2023 collapses found enforcement gaps and amnesty provisions meant even post-1999 buildings could be retroactively legalized despite code violations, and that some contractors altered approved structural plans after inspection sign-off. Building age and permit history alone do not confirm compliance with current seismic design standards.
dead_ends.condition: Applies to buildings anywhere in Turkey's seismically active regions, not only the 2023 earthquake zone

workarounds.action: Request or commission an independent 'riskli yapi' (risky-building) structural assessment through a Ministry-licensed institution under Law No. 6306, rather than relying on the occupancy permit alone
workarounds.how: Building owners or occupants can apply to an engineering firm, university, professional chamber office, or other institution licensed by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change to carry out a structural risk survey (site/soil study plus load-bearing-system inspection); the resulting 'riskli yapi' determination is independent of the building's permit history.

workarounds.action: Before renting, buying, or staying long-term, consult a licensed structural/civil engineer for an independent opinion rather than relying on a landlord's or seller's assurances about the building's permit status
workarounds.tradeoff: An independent assessment costs money and takes time, and is most practical for longer stays or property purchases rather than short tourist visits.
